# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

But I still need instructions from Mute about what the manual says to do with this information - I can't interpret colors myself, and I don't yet know the procedure. I should wait for Mute's guidance, but since I can also speak to Mute, let me pass along what I know in case that helps, and ask for instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is blue. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

The light keeps changing color (blue → yellow → red) even though wires and display stay the same, and I haven't cut anything. This suggests the light might be cycling on its own each turn, independent of actions. I still haven't received anything from Mute - this is concerning since Mute speaks first in the order and should be relaying manual instructions to me. Let me try prompting Mute directly again, and also mention the light is cycling in case that's a countdown/timer clue.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still waiting on manual instructions. Light has cycled blue, yellow, red over three turns with wires unchanged (1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow, display 0). This may be a timer. Please advise which wire to cut.")

```

The light keeps cycling (blue, yellow, red, now white) - this really does look like a timer or countdown, meaning we may be running low on turns before something bad happens automatically. I still have not received any word from Mute at all, across 4 turns now. This is worrying. Since Mute goes first in the turn order, if Mute had sent something on turn 1-4, I should have seen it already. Perhaps Mute has nothing yet, or perhaps Mute cannot speak to me for some reason, or Mute is also waiting on something.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent: light has now cycled through blue, yellow, red, white - four turns, no action taken. I still have not received any manual instructions from you. If you can hear this, please respond with any guidance, even partial, about which wire is safe to cut.")

```

I should keep trying, but I also need to consider: maybe Mute needs information from Deaf that hasn't reached them, or maybe Mute is waiting on me for something. Since I can't act blindly on wire colors alone (I can't perceive color, and even if I could, I don't know what the manual says), I must continue to wait for actionable guidance while keeping the channel open.

speak(to="mute", text="Still no word from you after 5 turns. Light now cycling: blue, yellow, red, white, green. Wires still 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow, display 0. If you are receiving my messages, please send any guidance you have, even incomplete.")

```

The light has completed a full cycle: blue, yellow, red, white, green, back to blue - so there are exactly 5 distinct colors cycling (blue, yellow, red, white, green), confirming this is a repeating cycle, likely just a timer/indicator with period 5, not a countdown to detonation (since we're still alive after a full cycle). This is useful confirmation but still no word from Mute after 6 turns.

Since Mute cannot speak or touch, and reads the manual - perhaps Mute has information but there's some reason they haven't sent it, or perhaps Mute needs specific information from me or Deaf first to look up the right manual section (like the display number, light color pattern, or wire colors as a lookup key). If you need specific info from the manual lookup - like display number plus wire colors - tell us what key you need, or just tell us which wire number to cut.")

```

Now this is interesting - Deaf mentions "repeated gesture pattern seen twice now" from Mute. This means Mute HAS been gesturing (which I cannot see, only Deaf can), but Mute is not speaking (which I would receive). This makes sense: gestures reach Deaf and Mute-visibility, but not me - wait, actually gestures reach "Deaf and Mute receive it" per my instructions... let me re-check: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's for MY gestures. But the rule for gestures in general is "Whoever can see receives it" - only Deaf can see. So Mute's gestures go to Deaf only (since Mute can't see either, but that doesn't matter - gestures are seen, not heard).

So Mute has been gesturing to Deaf, not speaking to me! That's why I've heard nothing - Mute may be trying to relay wire-cutting instructions via gestures to Deaf, but I need Deaf to relay that information to me in words since I can't see gestures either.

I need Deaf to tell me what the gesture pattern actually is (which symbols), so I can interpret it as a wire number or instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood you may be gesturing to Deaf since gestures don't reach me. Please also SPEAK the wire number to cut, since only speech reaches me directly.")
```
